Key results regarding the relationship between group actions on locally compact second-countable spaces and their orbit equivalence, specifically concerning virtually cyclic groups, have significant implications. They extend previously established knowledge on finite group actions, revealing that geodesic actions on specific Banach spaces and the group $H^2(\mathbb{R})$ exhibit this property, while also showing the existence of countably infinite virtually cyclic groups whose geodesic actions on $\mathbb{S}^1$ cannot be conjugated.

Given a set of observations from a probability measure and projection operators that define subsets within an infinite-dimensional space, we seek the conditional mean of another variable, given that it belongs to such a subset. This task is particularly challenging when the expectation operator does not have a simple, parameter-based representation. We introduce a method for estimating the conditional mean under these constraints, proving that these estimates converge at certain rates under specified conditions. These results apply to several practical cases, such as determining the average age of a U.S. worker within certain income brackets.

To establish that an epidemic model's state can be accurately assessed, we propose an linear observation predictor that relies on inherent process dynamics and infected population data within a limited area over a period of time in discrete-time.

In our research, we investigate the application of elaborate static graph
neural network models for predicting links within temporal knowledge graphs, 
where the existing relationships among entities are already sufficient for 
this purpose. We propose a novel static subgraph filtering technique that 
identifies and removes superfluous entities and properties from the training 
data, resulting in a more compact graph structure that exhibits 
significant 
performance gains without compromising the accuracy of predicting links in 
temporal knowledge graphs during testing. This strategy is validated through 
comprehensive experiments on several real-world datasets, which show that the 
refined models achieve accuracy nearly equivalent to that of more 
streamlined models, but, in predicting temporal links, exhibit a substantial 
parameter reduction, reaching up to 90% less parameters compared to the 
baseline model. We provide the implementation of our approach in an open-source 
format at https://github.com/hamidabdulbarr/TEKGP-static-link-prediction.

Research into ultrafast Kerr-lens mode-locking (KLKM) lasers has been a prominent area of study in recent years, driven by the challenge of increasing pulse peak power while maintaining the stability of the mode-locked state. In high-power KLKM lasers, maintaining stability is particularly difficult, as it relies heavily on mode-matching between the gain medium and the cavity lenses. This paper provides a detailed theoretical analysis of Kerr-lens stability in high-power regimes, incorporating important factors like thermal lens effects, astigmatism, diffraction, gain medium aperture, and gain-guiding. It is demonstrated that only by considering all these factors can the Kerr-lens stability range be calculated accurately. Furthermore, methods for enhancing the stability range and designing robust, aperture-tolerances Kerr-lens mode-locking lasers are discussed.

Online machine learning algorithms are designed to process data as it becomes available in real-time. However, handling high volumes of incoming data with these algorithms poses significant computational challenges. To alleviate this data can be segmented and processed concurrently in parallel, using a technique called Asynchronous Online Learning. Although effective, the Asynchronous Online Learning approach has limitations, particularly when processing data on resource-limited devices. To address these challenges, researchers propose an innovative technique called Asynchronous Resource Conscious Asynchronous Online Federated Learning (ARCAOL). This approach integrates the principles of Federated Learning and leverages multiple processing units to process data on mobile devices more efficiently. By leveraging local data and optimizing the use of processing resources, ARCAOL achieves improved performance and reduced model training times while maintaining privacy and security. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of ARCAOL and highlight its potential to revolutionize real-time machine learning data processing.

We've investigated how a back photonic crystal layer can enhance absorption in thin silicon layers by simulating its effect using the transfer-matrix method. The results show that introducing a back photonic crystal layer significantly increases absorption in the anti-guiding configuration over a wide spectrum, particularly under low-guiding conditions where absorption in the near-infrared and near-infrared ranges is increased. The transfer-matrix method results closely match those from a full 3D finite-difference time-domain simulation, validating our conclusions. The simulations reveal that the improved absorption is largely due to a wide-angle total internal reflection and point contact scattering. The optical properties of an ultrathin silicon layer coupled to a back photonic crystal layer were also explored.

u(x)$ and provides solutions to the equation $I_

u(x)) = a$, with an analysis of how the function behaves in the limit as $x$ approaches infinity.

We develop high dimensional extenders of any dimension d ≥ 1, applicable to vectors within the finite field $\mathbb{Z}_2^n$, encompassing a broad range of structures such as $t$-designs, $t$-wise independent functions, and $t$-approximate vector spaces. The height of these structures is governed by efficiency $\epsilon(n) = \lceil t \log_2 t + \dots \rceil$, allowing us to construct extender structures of large size utilizing cover constructions.

Within the family of 3d-4f-3d magnetic compounds, unique materials with exceptional magnetic properties can be identified. These ternary compounds, specifically perovskites and honeycomb-based compounds, possess an inverted band structure, allowing the possibility of achieving a magnetic state dominated by the transition metal, potentially giving rise to magnetic properties driven by the spin of the transition metal, as seen in antiferromagnets. This possibility is supported by theoretical calculations indicating that in honeycomb-based compounds with large, negative spin-orbit interactions, the magnetic moment contributed by the 3d electrons overcomes the suppression from the topological effect. As a result, honeycomb 3d-4f-3d compounds are promising to exhibit magnetic properties driven by the spin of the transition metal. To investigate this, a detailed study was conducted on GdInO$_{3}$, an exemplary antiferromagnet featuring a centered honeycomb lattice, where spin-orbit coupling plays a pivotal role. This study involved measuring the temperature-dependent in-plane and out-of-plane magnetization of GdInO$_{3}$ using a SQUID magnetometer, and comparing its in-plane magnetic response with that of the analogous compound, GdCuO$_{3}$. These measurements, coupled with theoretical predictions, revealed a significant spin of the 3d electrons in GdInO$_{3}$, thereby validating that three-dimensional magnetic properties can be generated through 3d electron

In large networks where sparse, many nodes remain unconnected, traditional methods for representing nodes fall short in accurately predicting missing connections. Our research introduces a new approach called SSNE (Sparse Stochastic Network Embedding) for rapidly computing node representations suitable for link prediction, especially in large, sparse networks. By building upon the success of stochastic proximity embedding, we addressed two main limitations: first, we overcame rapid computation times by introducing an efficient force model based on pairwise interactions, similar to gravitational forces, allowing us to apply the techniques from Google's TensorFlow-distributed for parallel processing. Our second improvement lies in a novel force direction model that takes into account node similarity in directions away from each other. This enables the method to handle sparse networks where connections are more likely to be found away from each other node. Our approach allows for predicting links by analyzing the movements of nodes during representation learning. Our experiments demonstrate that SSNE achieves state-of-the-art results on both dense and sparse networks for predicting links using sparse data sets.

Deep silicon micro-fabricated vapor cells and their counterparts in DKM material are employed in a Doppler atom interferometer to develop integrated atom optics. Specifically, the micro-fabricated interferometer uses these microstructured vapor cells and KDM-doped silicon to optimize the interaction between atomic vapor and light-balls made of silicon, thus enabling scalable improvements to integrated atom interferometry.

To accurately predict the Distortion to Noise Ratio under various conditions, the Distortion Power Nonlinearity Model was created using the Generalized Memoryless Model. It involved a two-step process where a power function fitted the Nonlinear Distortion Power Surface in the frequency domain with high precision under 99.9% probability conditions. Notably, due to the symmetry properties of the power function, only a portion of the power surface parameters needed to be optimized. Furthermore, the validity of the power function fit was confirmed through the calculation of the Root Mean Square Error, showing minimal errors in all tested scenarios, thus validating the model's accuracy. It was also found that the error surface of the power function has a unique minimum point, a valuable finding that can be used to simplify the optimization process in power model training.

Wildfires significantly impact ecosystems, human lives, and property, causing extensive damage and destruction. Recent studies indicate a direct correlation between wildfires and global warming. Recent advancements in deep learning technologies have enabled the creation of sophisticated systems that can detect and forecast wildfires. Nevertheless, existing approaches have several drawbacks such as inaccurate classifications and premature alarm raising. To address these limitations, we introduce FIRe-GAN, a cutting-edge deep learning framework, designed to efficiently identify active wildfires in aerial images captured by various sensors such as infrared, visible, and multispectral cameras on drones and satellites in near real-time. Our innovative framework capitalizes on its ability to combine information from diverse image sources and enhance the accuracy of wildfire detection. Our model is trained using a comprehensive dataset of over 15,000 wildfire and non-wildfire images. Our framework's performance was rigorously evaluated against cutting-edge state-of-the-art models and demonstrated superior accuracy. Our framework's source code and related datasets are publicly accessible for research purposes.

Depression affects many people worldwide and causes significant impairment in their daily lives. The widespread use of social media offers an opportunity to study this growing health concern by leveraging online interactions as a potential indicator of depression. By analyzing social media posts, researchers can create algorithms to identify individuals exhibiting signs of depression, potentially allowing for timely intervention. However, developing effective detection algorithms requires datasets that accurately reflect individuals' emotional states, which in turn enables researchers to evaluate their algorithms' performance. This study outlines the process of constructing a social media dataset by collaborating with individuals experiencing depression, along with an analysis of the associated challenges.

This paper delves into the characteristics of a random graph model, consisting of $n$ vertices, where each vertex is assigned to one of several compartments following the SIR model commonly used to simulate an epidemic. Edges between the vertices are deemed present with a probability that varies according to the SARS-CoV-2 transmission rate and the numbers of susceptible, infectious, and susceptible populations. As the number of vertices approaches infinity, the model is demonstrated to converge to a limiting object, revealing the emergence of a giant component. Various aspects of the model are analyzed in detail.

This study provides the first computational analysis of the isoscalar giant monopole resonance (ISGMR) in 24Mg and 28Si within the random phase approximation incorporating the direct, exchange, correlation, and coupling of isoscalar monopole and quadrupole collective motions. The results of our analysis show that the predicted energies for the ISGMR in the excitations comprising 0+ states align with the experimental data more accurately than those involving 4+ states. Furthermore, the predicted ISGMR energies are slightly overestimated, but the predicted widths agree closely with the experimental values, demonstrating an emphasis on the role of coupling between isoscalar monopole and quadrupole collective motions in the decay process.

This paper examines the stick-slip phenomenon in systems governed by Coulomb friction through a globally stabilizing feedback mechanism. A case study involving a pure transport system highlights the significance of addressing stick-slip oscillations, particularly when attempting to achieve convergence to a target state within a finite timeframe. Our findings demonstrate that for certain strictly robust systems, convergence to the target state is actually feasible using feedback mechanisms that result in singular equations when velocity and its derivative are both zero.

A novel neural network-based approach to solving stochastic Markov Decision Processes has been developed, specifically within the insurance sector. Traditional methods in this sector often prioritize simplicity and robustness, but can compromise solution quality and system stability. Unlike these traditional methods, our approach does not necessitate an explicit estimation of the Bellman operator, which could be computationally challenging or infeasible in some cases. This deep learning method is versatile and can be stacked to tackle the problems associated with gradient-free methods, which are commonly used in robust optimization. We applied it to two key tasks: maximizing expected profit and minimizing the probability of insolvency under considerable uncertainty. The effectiveness of our approach has been validated through real-world applications, which demonstrate superior performance over traditional methods while providing an interpretable framework.

This research introduces a pioneering approach to incorporate user intent extraction in sequential recommender systems. To achieve this, we suggest an innovative architecture called the Latent User Purpose Module (LUPM), which integrates with existing sequential models to predict sequences of items. Distinguishing itself from current methods that rely on explicit user feedback, LUPM analyzes the outcomes of a user's interactions to derive a high-level intent and measures it using BERT, a pre-trained language model. By employing a multi-modal approach that combines visual and auditory features, we demonstrate the efficacy of our method on two prominent benchmark datasets for movie and book recommendations. Notably, our approach achieves exceptional results in predicting sequences of related items by capturing and assessing user intent from the outcomes of their actions.

We investigate the estimation of low-rank matrices when given n observations that are product of matrices drawn from known probability distributions but are subject to multiplicative noise of varying distributions across different dimensions. This framework encompasses diverse applications such as incomplete matrix reconstruction, factor analysis, and clustering in high-dimensional data. Focusing on the case where noise distribution is consistent but varies across dimensions, we establish lower and upper bounds on estimation error for certain types of estimators based on empirical posterior, considering specific probability distributions and showing that these achieve optimal performance in many instances. This research extends existing work by allowing for anisotropic noise distributions and non-standard probability distributions typical in clustering problems. Our analysis employs the singular value perturbation bound to derive the error of an optimal estimator and employs stochastic independence to bound the estimation error of an empirical posterior. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the derived bounds are often tight and often achieve optimal convergence rates up to a logarithmic factor.

We present a novel topological system that exhibits inherent stability without reliance on symmetry or average Hamiltonian structure. Initially, our model is formulated as a four-band system anchored by a non-Hermitian unitary matrix, which critically depends on a newly identified constraint. We then reduce this framework to two essential components: a four-dimensional system exhibiting inherent topological stability and a two-dimensional system with an arbitrary mean structure. Our analysis reveals that the topological characteristics in two dimensions are a direct consequence of these underlying components. Furthermore, our model is successfully applied to experimental data, with observed properties aligning perfectly with our theoretical predictions.

The ratio of semi-inclusive Lepton Universalities, involving electron-muon and muon-tau pairs, is introduced as a valuable tool for probing new physics beyond the standard model at specific $q^2$ ranges. A novel ratio, based on semi-inclusive dilepton differential cross sections, was formulated to compare $b\to s\ell\ell$ and $b\to c\ell\ell$ transitions. These ratios exhibit minimal dependence on non-perturbative effects, making them ideal for extracting the CKM ratio $|\eta_E| = V_{tb}^*V_{ts}/V_{tb}^*V_{tc}$ in $b\to s\ell\ell$ transitions. First-order QCD corrections were computed for these ratios and found to significantly reduce their dependence on the renormalization scale. Additionally, the proposed ratios were found to have minimal sensitivity to power corrections. Current experimental results from the LHCb collaboration were used to constrain several ratios and indicate that the $\mathcal{R}_{5<q^2<8}$ ratio, which is sensitive to Wilson coefficients $C_9$ and $C_{10}$, is in good agreement with the standard model. On the other hand, the $\mathcal{R_{II}}$ ratio, which compares $b\to s\ell\ell$ and $b\to c\ell\ell$ transitions, was found to be in slight tension

This research aims to develop a distributed solution for controlling networked linear systems, incorporating changes in parameters through efficient design principles. We outline a distributed strategy for creating linear controllers and observability distributors, ensuring digital implementation with reduced computational costs, followed by a distributed method for adjusting the system's distributed structure, optimizing its performance and stability margins. We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach in solving consensus problems within linear systems under changing parameters using simulation-based examples.

Since the COVID-19 pandemic's onset, significant research has focused on developing computational tools to detect and track its spread. Previous studies have applied various machine learning techniques to model COVID-19's clinical and radiological presentations. However, proposed models often demand diverse datasets and complex computational frameworks. In response, a novel two-stage classification approach based on BERT is introduced, leveraging the model's transfer learning capabilities to minimize data requirements and simplify implementation. This method's effectiveness is demonstrated through evaluation on external benchmark datasets containing COVID-19, Lung Opacity, and Viral Pneumonia images. Experimental results compare the proposed approach with existing solutions and showcase its superior performance.

This article offers an overview of cutting-edge techniques for analyzing complex networks, highlighting cutting-edge research in a rapidly advancing field. Given the rapidly evolving nature of network science, with groundbreaking research being published at a rapid pace, we aim to be comprehensive while acknowledging the inherent challenges in selecting the most promising methods and approaches within this dynamic environment.

The study of how different entities and systems adapt and interact within various scales of time, known as eco-evolutionary dynamics, is a growing field of complexity science. This concept is challenging due to its broad definition and the difficulty in distinguishing between evolutionary interactions at different rates. To make progress, we suggest that eco-evolutionary dynamics should be examined through the lens of deep time theory, focusing on their unique properties, patterns, and distinct features. By using control theory, we argue that these processes can be understood as a competition between two opposing forces, evolution and non-evolution, whose interactions determine whether they are truly eco-evolutionary. This dynamic competition involves a continuous back-and-forth struggle between these forces, influenced by environmental conditions and the complexity of the systems involved. By exploring the history of these interactions and the factors that contribute to them, we can identify the distinctive features of eco-evolutionary dynamics and the conditions necessary for their emergence.

Recent self-supervised learning approaches for speech do not rely on labeled data, but can be vulnerable to optimization attacks, according to a new discovery. A novel attack technique, called Adversarial Acoustic Matching Attack (AAMA), targets self-supervised learning models by directly attacking a teacher model to mislead a student model's training. AAMA achieves a higher success rate than current techniques designed to attack supervised speech models. Furthermore, a signal-to-distortion ratio (SDR)-based metric was proposed to gauge the effectiveness of attacks. AAMA's performance suggests that the susceptibility of speech self-supervised learning to these attacks could indicate a reliable metric for assessing the potential risk in real-world applications.

This study focuses on understanding user adoption of decentralized, blockchain-driven cryptocurrency exchanges by applying the combined frameworks of the Knowledge Process Chain and the Technology Acceptance Model. By doing so, we aim to shed light on the primary drivers of users embracing DEXs and identify the gaps in existing literature to further the field of blockchain research. Through a comprehensive online survey, we collected and analyzed data from 390 users who have experience with DEXs, resulting in structural equation modeling analysis that reveals knowledge process chains have a significant impact on users' actual usage of DEXs, with Performance Expectancy being the most influential factor.

A new method is developed to evaluate the analysis robustness against biases in case-control studies, particularly in scenarios with missing data. The method employs Talmi's sensitivity analysis, enhanced by a sensitivity measure known as the E-value, estimated through multiple imputation techniques. The sensitivity results are statistically characterized through confidence intervals and comparison statistics in a multiple-imputation framework. The proposed approach theory and practice consistency is examined through numerical simulations and a real-world cancer study example highlighting the importance of considering bias risks in data analysis despite complete case analysis showing significant results.

We provide a list of all possible ways to extend the bounded region of a specific quantum algebra to the entire complex plane, preserving a specific algebraic structure, and we show that this list is exhaustive. Notably, one particular extension corresponds to the traditional surface S, described by the Poncelet theorem, which can be represented through algebraic relations involving trigonometric functions, although these are projections of holomorphic relations involving elliptic functions in the context of the Poncelet theorem.

The Internet of Vehicles has created opportunities for collaborative learning models to enhance safety and convenience. Federated learning, a key model, enables vehicle sharing for specific tasks while protecting user privacy, but concerns over data security persist due to potential privacy breaches and malicious attacks on the training process. To address these challenges, integrating emerging blockchain technology into federated learning systems has emerged as a promising solution for secure, private, and reliable data exchange, user authentication, resource management, and trust establishment in collaborative learning. This review aims to provide a comprehensive analysis of recent advancements in integrating blockchain and federated learning in Internet of Vehicles scenarios, exploring use cases, architectures, security protocols, and performance metrics through a structured framework of categorization and performance evaluation.

Allegedly, the ALICE Collaboration at the CERN pp collider, a dataset gathered at 5.02 TeV, has provided an analysis of 100 pb^-1 of prompt and B-meson associated charm production using the rapidity range -2 < y < 2. The analysis encompassed both electron-hadron and di-hadron correlation measurements, and the results are compared with theoretical models and previous experiments, particularly focusing on B-meson associated charm production in the same rapidity range for the first time, and the findings are also relevant to understanding heavy-ion interactions.

A large cryogenic system has been created and is now in operation at the Fermilab and LNS Sites. This system is specifically designed to support quantum computing initiatives by utilizing superconducting transmon qubits. Composed of three stages, the cryogenic system includes stages cooled by Ni/Au V-shaped helix plateaus and He-3 adiabatic demagnetization refrigerators, reaching temperatures as low as 30 millikelvin. At the quantum computing initiative site, 30 gates based on superconducting transqubits are integrated and connected via 5,000 coaxial cables and 1,000 flux pins, forming a total of 3000000 connections.

In many systems that rely on cryptographic security, improper use of cryptographic algorithms is frequently the cause of the issue. This study examines and categorizes novel attacks that exploit vulnerabilities arising from misconfigurations of established cryptographic tools. Specifically, we identify and analyze a single attack vector that encompasses three distinct misconfigurations and results in a total of 10 highly impactful security vulnerabilities across six popular Python cryptography libraries. To promote better cryptographic practices, we develop an educational framework that promotes six core cryptographic principles. Furthermore, we develop a suite of educational materials and a Python-based cryptographic evaluation tool that enables users to identify vulnerabilities of this type in Python code. Our analysis reveals that our approach is effective, as demonstrated by its application to real-world Python projects, where we successfully detected 10 significant security flaws.

Tagged images serve as the foundation for many computer vision applications, but the labor-intensive process of manually annotating image content hinders their widespread use. In this work, we present a definitive benchmark that sets the current state-of-the-art in automated tagging. By combining different tagging algorithms and utilizing a democratic voting system, our method can handle a vast number of images with high accuracy. Notably, our approach does not rely on any pre-annotated labeling, thus avoiding the propagation of errors. The proposed method can handle extremely large datasets, comprising over a billion images, containing more than 150,000 tags. The system's design allows it to scale efficiently in parallel, achieving substantial tagging in a relatively short period.

Seismic reflectivity inversion plays a crucial role in oil and gas exploration by reconstructing underground structures. However, the assumption of uniformly spaced reflectors is overly restrictive. Instead, we approach the reflectivity reconstruction problem as a nonuniform sparse inversion problem. Unlike previous symmetrical inversion methods, we propose a Proximal Average Network (SPAN), a symmetrical network that is effective for both ascending and descending sparse non-zero elements. Additionally, we reformulate proxy-based reconstruction into a joint sparse recovery problem and improve convergence using an adaptive step-size. Numerical results demonstrate that our proposed method is superior to existing techniques.

This article investigates the semigroups of composition operators on BMOA-like spaces, specifically focusing on when the semigroups of $T_t$ and $Q\_T\_t$ contain any non-zero operators. In this context, $BMOA\_p$ denotes the subspace of-BMOA with analytic functions whose $p$-th derivative belongs to BMO, and $Q\_T\_t$ is a transformed version of $T\_t$ involving the quotient of $T\_t$'s second to first derivative.

We introduce a general method for computing the scaling dimensions and fusion rules of a unitary rational CFT using the finite-size spectrum of its corresponding DDD model. Our analysis reveals that the scaling dimensions of primary fields and their corresponding Kac labels are interrelated by a universal scaling function that depends only on the central charge and the conformal dimension. This relationship enables a precise determination of the fusion rules by identifying a set of characteristic sign patterns within the coefficients of the 3-K symbol. These findings are further demonstrated by re-evaluating the scaling dimensions and fusion rules for the su(2)_3 model and a previously discovered non-diagonal unitary RCFT with a 600-dimensional Verlinde matrix and 6 generators. Notably, our computation of the scaling dimensions reveals that the minimal gap within each set of fields sharing the same scaling dimension is consistently identified by the Kac label with the smallest value. This result is verified by applying it to the Haagerup model, where we determine the scaling dimensions and fusion rules for its primary fields up to a central value of k=60, revealing that only two of its primary fields are affected when this central value increases. Our research also reveals that one of these primary fields, previously assigned label $\xi_{22}^2$, actually corresponds to Kac label $\xi_{12}$.

In the realm of natural language processing, accurately assigning part-of-speech (POS) tags to words is a fundamental challenge. Historically, the gold-standard annotation scheme, the Penn Treebank, has been used as a reference. However, many of its tags are ambiguous, leading to inconsistencies when researchers attempt to mark historically significant texts with this same scheme. They often have to make subjective decisions, which hampers the reliability of the process. 

To overcome this limitation, we propose a pioneering approach, where we acknowledge the inherent ambiguities of POS tags by representing them as sets. This allows us, for the first time, to reliably use the Penn Treebank's tags for historical texts. Our approach involves a novel neural framework that predicts the various acceptable tags for each word token. 

To evaluate the effectiveness of this approach, we conducted a large-scale, gold-standard annotation project involving 200 historically important texts spanning 200 years. Our experiments, spanning both tagged historical data and Wittenberg German, yielded significant results that outperformed traditional, single-set prediction methods in terms of tagging accuracy and led to notable improvements in downstream tasks like machine translation.

This research focuses on a class of integro-differential equations involving the integro-exponential kernel $k(x,y) = e^{-\frac{|x-y|^\alpha}{\alpha}}$, a special case of the Mat\'ern kernel widely used in geostatistics. Although previous studies on such equations have relied heavily on the fractional Laplacian, we take a different approach, examining solutions as generalized functions and integrating them with the help of the extensible exponential function. This method, facilitated by introducing a new convolution product, allows us to establish a suitable framework of spaces where solutions can be obtained in the sense of generalized functions. It also enables us to establish minimal regularity requirements for solutions and establish non continuity of solutions when the nonlinearity is superlinear, in contrast to existing literature on integro-differential equations, especially when influenced by fractional calculus.

City management is heavily reliant on maintaining up-to-date information, such as in their user-friendly requirements documents.
However, manually translating these documents into formal specifications for computer processing proves to be a highly time-consuming task.
To alleviate this issue, we have developed an intelligent city management assistant based on the global city ontology framework.
This city ontology framework is derived from the well-established DM ontology framework and provides a structured knowledge base for processing user inputs.
Our approach leverages pre-built knowledge and intelligent user interfaces to streamline the translation process between user inputs and global ontology formalisms.
This intelligent assistant significantly reduces the time required for users to maintain their requirements and enhances the overall efficiency of communication between various city management systems.

This paper presents a refined version of the hidden inverses protocol for correcting bit-flip errors, which is then tested on the surface code architecture using superconducting circuits. The modified protocol simplifies protocol depth from four to three, and incorporates real-world considerations, such as idle dephasing and imperfect measurements. Following this enhanced protocol, a simulated quantum circuit runs to examine recovery rates under various code distance configurations.

In a general category $\mathbb{E}$ with a basic form of logical reasoning, a preorder can be visually represented by the union of two sets of prior occurrences, whereas an equivalence relation is shown through the intersection of two prior occurrences, according to a basic form of visual composition. It follows that a preorder can be expressed as a subset of an equivalence relation when the visual composition rule is applied. Building upon a previous finding, we demonstrate that this statement holds true in all $\mathbb{E}$ with a basic form of visual composition and further, under specified conditions, with or without the assumption of non-zero results for a basic visual composition.

Using a statistical model known as the extreme value copula, we analyzed the relationship between two extreme weather events at specific marinas in Western Europe, including wave height and period. 

Data collected from the Port de la Juniette in the Bay of Biscay and Gijon in the Cantabrian Sea were used to examine joint wave height and period extremes. 

Our analysis included calculating return levels, assessing extreme weather return periods, and visualizing probability distributions. 

Results showed a strong correlation between extreme wave heights and periods, which varied depending on the location, and highlighted the utility of extreme value copulas in evaluating and predicting extreme weather conditions in marine environments.

Multimodal models that process text and images are gaining significant attention due to their exceptional zero-shot capabilities, but their performance is often hindered by their tendency to rely on non-visual characteristics, known as biases. To enhance these models' robustness against such biases, we employ adversarial training, aiming to produce text representations less susceptible to them. Unlike conventional approaches, our adversarial text does not attempt to conceal its authenticity but rather minimizes notable signs of bias, allowing us to generate biased-free captions. Consequently, visual-language pre-training becomes more centered around visually distinctive content, resulting in more refined visual representations that we call image features, more attentive to these visual nuances. As a result, our VT-CLIP model, which builds on top of CLIP and GPT-3.5, outperforms current state-of-the-art models in visual perception tasks, especially complex and challenging scenarios.

This paper presents an efficient method for providing noisy matrix solutions to operator switching equations, building on the development of iterative operators in 2020. The development of the splitting technique in that study was specifically for linear coupling systems of Stratonovich operator switching ODEs applicable to a narrow range of problems, resolving the issue of noise. By expanding the technique's scope to encompass general matrix systems with diverse noise types and accounting for operator transition matrices, our research extends the applicability of this approach. Furthermore, we establish a new integration formula for random matrices, an essential tool for proving convergence of the splitting method.

We identify the integers $n$ for which the $n$-th section functor of quaternions is linked to the $n$-th based map of quaternions. This reveals that the $n$-th section functor is equivalent to the $n$-th based map of quaternions when $n$ is divisible by 4; however, this equivalence does not hold for $n=2$. This discovery has significant implications for quaternionic Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectra. Notably, it is shown that $\sigma H_{\mathbb{Z}/2}^S$ does not embed into $\sigma S$ for suitably localized spectra, and a similar situation arises when replacing $S$ with $M\mathcal{K}$, the complex Klein bottle function spectrum. This has further implications for the $B$-field of quaternionic K-theory. Additionally, it is shown that the $B$-field of a certain cover of the mod 2 Arf invariant is nontrivial, which is equivalent to the Arf invariant itself. This is proven by examining its effect on the Arf invariant of links in a way that respects Arf invariant duality. This highlights a fundamental difference between Arf invariant duality and its complex K-theory counterpart, which relies on second Stiefel-Whitons.

Given a two-dimensional F-stable local F-finite Gorenstein ring R, we demonstrate the following: 
(a) There is a precise lower limit on the tight closure exponent (P) relative to the F-singularities of (R), specifically not exceeding 2 times F-regularity index (I). 
(b) A direct relationship exists between P and I when (R) exhibits a specific attribute (C). 
When (R) classifies as an equation-satisfying cluster, (a) simplifies to (P) being less than or equal to times I. 
When (R) classifies as an equation-satisfying cluster of characteristic zero, (a) simplifies to (P) being less than or equal to times I.

In the field of medical imaging, numerous tasks like detecting abnormalities in radiology or identifying cancer in pathology biopsies have been explored by researchers. The deployment of artificial intelligence-based methodologies in such tasks necessitates the availability of deeply nested classification systems and deeply ordered classification systems. To accommodate these requirements, the DICOM standard, specifically the Structured Document Transfer Format (SDOF), offers standardized methods for encoding transfer systems that are both nested and ordered. The DICOM standard, specifically in the context of radiology, has garnered considerable attention, whereas in pathology research, there has been a significant disparity in reporting standards. The introduction of highDICOM, a Python library for standardized encoding of image-related annotations in pathology research, is presented in this study. The library facilitates the creation of deeply nested classification systems and deeply ordered classification systems in line with DICOM standards, specifically in the context of radiology, by providing both deeply nested and ordered classification systems. The efficacy of the library is demonstrated through its application in a variety of research settings, including the analysis of deep learning-based methods in the diagnosis of colorectal cancer in biopsy samples.

In this study, the Bach tensor's quasi-local energy, momentum, and angular angular momentum are derived for four-dimensional asymptotically flat spacetimes, derived from the Einstein-Hilbert action's boundary term, revealing that these quantities depend on the metric near the boundary d2S. These conserved charges can be expressed as six-dimensional volume integrals and can be adapted for asymptotically flat spacetimes. Evaluating them on Schwarzschild black holes, we find their values to be proportional to mass and angular momentum. Furthermore, we explore the construction of a Virasoro algebra using the Brown-York stress tensor, considering the extrinsic curvature at the boundary, and discuss its implications. Lastly, we propose a Bekenstein-Hawking entropy expression in terms of the Bach tensor, valid for spherically symmetric black holes.

In recent years, deep learning has shown significant potential in analyzing DNA sequences. However, determining which features in these sequences are essential for a specific task remains a significant issue. We believe that learning these features independently of a specific task is key to achieving success. In an effort to address this challenge, we developed a method that can automatically extract DNA features without supervision. When applied to unsupervised learning, this method has outperformed other approaches. Furthermore, it has been discovered that a smaller set of genes, known as open-chromatin genes, is sufficient for encoding a DNA sequence's content and structure and even when used in a supervised task for binary classification, this method has outperformed other other methods.

The nature of the metal-insulator transition in $V_2O_3$(0001) is heavily influenced by various factors including structural, chemical, and environmental modifications. In our study, we examined how varying the number of layers, temperature and the application of tensile stress impact $V_2O_3$(0001) ultrathin films grown on single-crystal LaAlO$_3$(0001) substrates. Notably, we observed that an insufficient number of vanadium oxide layers, elevated temperatures and the presence of lattice constants exceeding 4.35~\AA\ all lead to the destabilization of the insulating phase in $V_2O_3$(0001). Notably, we found that this insulating phase can only be preserved within a specific range of film thickness, a temperature below 200~K, and a range of in-plane lattice constants that are less than 4.36~\AA. These findings are in line with our own previous research and those conducted by other groups using different experimental methods and ultrathin film growth techniques, thus highlighting the importance of carefully controlling the structural and environmental factors in order to study the metal-insulator transition in $V_2O_3$(0001) ultrathin films.

The Clebsch canonization of smooth Poisson manifolds can be locally achieved through finite transformations, according to a generalization of Lie-Poisson systems. Specifically, a particular set of coordinates exists locally where the Poisson bracket simplifies to a certain form, involving terms that depend on functions and their derivatives. This form is particularly noteworthy as it resembles a magnetic Hamiltonian system with a gauge field proportional to a constant. The proof presented here utilizes Lie's theory of groups and Lie algebras to establish this result, along with a characterization of the atlas needed to cover the manifold with this simplified form. Additionally, a relationship between the characteristic distributions of the manifold and certain subalgeles of the Lie algebra is revealed. By association, the Poisson bracket in question corresponds to certain right-invariant vector fields on the group, enabling further investigation into the properties of the manifold and its symmetries.

Based on data from the Korean Microlensing Titanet Project, a team of researchers identified 51 instances of gravitational microlensing anomalies, occurring in 44 systems and observed within the KMTNet's 2018 secondary fields. Of these planets, 19 exhibited notable anomalies in light curves, categorized under Class I and II, and research into their mass and orbital properties revealed a spectrum ranging from super-Earths to Neptunes. Notably, the detected planets align with previously established correlations, specifically regarding the relationship between their mass and orbital separation. However, the researchers observed discrepancies in another correlation, which states a correlation between a planet's mass and its eccentricity, and these discrepancies challenge a previously proposed hypothesis regarding eccentricity. Furthermore, the researchers discuss the significance of their findings in relation to exoplanet detection methods and their implications for exoplanet population models.

A series of papers aimed at reducing the computational complexity of solving fundamental fluid dynamics equations through characteristic finite element methods has been published. Conical domains are considered in this line of research due to the ease of deriving analytical solutions for a simplified 1D wave equation. This new set of simulations demonstrates how introducing a non-conservative flux into the balance equations enables better control of local mesh refinement, thereby increasing efficiency. These improved schemes are able to maintain nearly constant or even reduced mesh sizes compared to conventional methods, such as those based on the Lax-Wendro夫 approach. Notably, a new scheme, known as the Runge-Kutta Discontinuous method, offers an even lower computational cost. Overall, these advancements enable solving complex 2D and 3D problems with significantly smaller meshes.

A prominent 2018 study utilizing natural language processing examined the impact of loan descriptions on underwriting decisions, revealing descriptors such as purpose and frequency to be crucial in decision-making. Yet, recent changes in mortgage loan applications due to the pandemic necessitate reevaluating the importance of these factors. This study aims to evaluate the performance of various machine learning models - Random Forest, Gradient Boosted Trees, and Neural Networks - using data from the Big Data Bank Network, a large collection of Italian loan information. We investigate the evolution of these models over time and analyze their respective characteristics to identify essential loan attributes for accurate decision-making.

We introduce a conjecture that expresses the chromatic symmetric functions of certain "tame" Dyck trails in a form similar to the basis for q-rook theory. Building on this, we show that the chromatic symmetric functions of tangent and divergence patterns can be exactly determined in a formulaic representation related to q-rook theory. These findings offer the first instances where the chromatic symmetric functions of these patterns have been quantified in terms of symmetry elements.

In the realm of computer vision, deep convolutional networks excel at extracting features from images. Conventional convolutions are adept at capturing spatial relationships among pixels, but fail to discern directional relationships, a crucial aspect in certain vision tasks. To address this gap, a novel convolutional network operator, termed 'direction convolution,' has been developed to effectively capture spatial patterns in directional aspects. The direction convolution operator utilizes an orientation map, derived from image gradients, to perform convolutions along specified directions. Experimental results using synthetic datasets and real-world images demonstrate that direction convolutions can learn more discerning directional features. Furthermore, a network architecture incorporating both orientation and direction convolutions achieves superior performance in single-view object detection tasks and significantly outperforms conventional networks in stereo depth perception tasks.

We use the oscillatory integral approach to establish a novel relative trace formula in $Sp_4(\mathbb{A})$, where $\mathbb{A}$ represents the adelic ring of a rational number field. This formula connects the automorphic representation theory with the representation categories of two curved linear groups composed of symplectic groups of dimensions 2 and 4, specifically $GL_2(\mathbb{A})$ and $H^+ = \{g \in Sp_4(\mathbb{A}) : {g\,g^{\vee}} = I\}$. The group $H^+$ can be viewed as a Loosely Semi-Simple Algebraic Group (LSAG) and, consequently, its representation theory is a fundamental aspect of our investigation, which also includes constructing a metaplectic cover of $H^+$. Furthermore, an application of this formula enables us to derive a novel identity linking Hecke eigenforms of weight 12 with even parity on $\SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and representations in $H^+$.

Using amplitude subgroups, we investigate all irreducible representations of $SU(3)_F$, and find that the differences in the calculated top quark mass across various flavor representations are substantial, ranging from 1.5 to 2 GeV. This represents a 0.1-0.2% variation, surpassing the anticipated top quark mass precision of 0.067 GeV from a future top factory. Notably, the mass representation 210 of $SU(3)_F$ yields the most accurate top quark mass with the smallest correction. Moreover, representations such as 21, 15, and 6 are sub-representations of 210, and, given a vanishing electric charge for the top quark, the lightest top quark mass is estimated to be the average of the quark masses in representations 21, 15, and 6, namely the average of $d$, $s$, and $t$ quark masses, namely 2.995 GeV.

We focus on $\chi$-bounded subgraph-tienting games played on graphs with maximum degree $\Delta$, given that the graph's edge chromatic number equals $\Delta$. In this game, Alice and Bob take turns altering a single edge's color, with Alice starting uncolored edges and passing turns to Bob once all edges have been assigned a color. Alice aims to use as few as possible total colors, whereas Bob aims to require Alice to use as many as possible total colors for each edge. It has been shown that when played on certain types of $\Delta$-regular graphs, Bob can force Alice to use as many as $\sqrt{\Delta}$ different colors. In contrast, we found nearly always-win strategies for Alice in the game when played on a broad range of graph types characterized by small maximum cycle lengths or maximum edge-colouring index of 3, resulting in Alice winning with just 2 or 3 colors.

We establish a hypercontractive inequality in a weighted Bergman space for functions defined on the unit ball in $\mathbb{C}^d$ with the following weight $w_\alpha(z)=\exp\left(-\frac{2}{(1-|z|^2)^{\sigma}}\right)$ where the parameters satisfy $0<\alpha<\frac{1}{2}$ and $0\le\sigma<\frac{1}{2}$, under a weighted Berman framework.

The COVID-19 pandemic has caused significant loss of life and long-term health issues worldwide, prompting researchers to focus on developing pulmonary diagnostic tools. To address the challenge of early detection under low-dose conditions, where image clarity may be compromised, we investigated a two-stage time-distributed capsule network. This innovative approach integrates deep learning and capsule networks to efficiently utilize available data. The first stage filters out noisy images, while the second stage performs accurate image classification. To compensate for any initial errors, we incorporated a correction module. To showcase the effectiveness of this novel method, we applied it to a large dataset of low-dose and high-dose CT scans and found it outperformed other approaches, delivering diagnoses comparable to those of expert radiologists under low-dose conditions.

This research focuses on organizing and optimizing space in low Earth orbit. The problem of packing in low Earth orbit can be compared to packing items of different sizes into a limited three-dimensional space efficiently, while minimizing wasted space. The study in question reveals that in low Earth orbit, various structures are used by at least five times as often as others. The different frames in low Earth orbit are being used for a range of purposes, including the deployment of solar panels, collecting space debris, and testing new methods of navigation. The research was carried out to a certain extent by employing a computer program that simulates various packing methods in low Earth orbit. The outcome of this simulation was the identification of the structures with the highest frequency, the determination of their usage in different applications, and the analysis of their potential for improvement. The findings from this simulation were further supported by the review of the technical literature and the assessment of the space organization methods currently used in low Earth orbit. The research also provides a few suggestions for enhancing these organization methods. The space organization methods in low Earth orbit can be further improved by the deployment of novel packing methods, the use of modular and reconfigurable structures, and the application of sustainable materials. The paper concludes with the presentation of the most effective organization methods and the proposal of future research directions.

We introduce a novel approach for automatically creating high-quality, topologically precise quadrilateral meshes of CAD models using integer linear programming. By formulating mesh generation as an optimization problem, our implicit mesh operator maximizes overall mesh quality and adheres to the model's topological constraints. The optimization variables, representing a dual grid, integer coordinates, and a cutting field, define a partial grid. To transform this partial grid into a complete coarse quadrilateral mesh, we leverage graph theory, specifically representing the cutting field as directed graphs and partitioning them into disjoint cycles. By iteratively solving corresponding flow problems, we partition the graphs and partition the cutting field accordingly to generate the coarse mesh from partial grid input. The proposed method's performance is validated through extensive testing on various 2D 45-element CAD models, demonstrating its ability to generate high-quality quadrilateral meshes with minimal warping ratios.

The sample correlation coefficient offers a valuable method for examining the linear relationship between two variables. However, its distribution is complex and difficult to analyze, especially when considering high-dimensional samples. This study derives precise mathematical expressions for the sample moments of the sample correlation coefficient under various data arrangements, revealing that higher-order moments become increasingly intricate. It also demonstrates how to compute the sample moments without determining the full probability density function.

The underlying S-matrix framework of scattering amplitudes in general gravitational theories is examined. A key assumption lies in contact interactions, which are typically non-zero and necessitate additional parameters in traditional approaches. However, in theories like string theory and Gauged Skyrme model, such contact terms vanish at low energies, enabling a low-gravity expansion without corresponding interaction constants. Furthermore, an investigation is conducted on the potential connections between high-gravity limits in standard QFT and low-gravity limits in unconventional theories, with a focus on the relationships between string theory and the Galilean Gravity. Additionally, an exploration is initiated on the possibility of an S-matrix formulation for gauge theories, specifically U(1) gauge theory.

We offer a novel Brézis-Hildebrandt type stabilization strategy to solve an unsolved issue in the literature, to find a finite-dimensional interior feedback control that ensures the solution of the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with a control, a critical initial value problem's equivalent solution. The control's effectiveness in achieving global stability has been proven in multiple studies, including works by H. Liu, Y. Liu and others, which established the validity of the control in ensuring the solution's asymptotic stability towards the zero solution, in cases where the control is designed to ensure the solution's stability in various spaces such as the $L^q$ Sobolev and Besov spaces.

LitMind is a lexicographical database incorporating dictionary-like entries,
particularly focusing on character-driven plot elements and their contextual
meanings, which are essential to understanding the central narrative of literary
works. Organized in a hierarchical classification system akin to the thesaurus
 Paradigm, LitMind comprises 17 distinct categories and approximately 200,000
 term entries available in over 100 languages. Each entry will be continuously
 supplemented through collaborative contributions from contributors utilizing
 the LitMind contributor interface.

The LIME method, originally created for machine learning models, has been adapted for recommendation systems to enhance transparency and trust in algorithms. However, the original explanations provided by LIME for these models lack consistency across similar items, which can be crucial for users to grasp the model's reasoning. In this paper, we present LIME-RS, a variant of LIME tailored for recommendation systems that incorporates consistency into its explanations. By merging the original approach with a variant of the epsilon-insensitivity method, LIME-RS offers a set of locally similar items and their respective scores, enabling a locally tailored "what-if" exploration for items within and beyond the top list generated by the recommendation model. Through case studies, we illustrate the benefits of our approach in enhancing the interpretability of deep learning models and demonstrate its capacity to expose potential biases in these models.

Researchers have developed and experimentally validated a computational framework to investigate the intricate relationships between various physical properties of a quantum framework, including its electronic level structure, well depth modifications, and band shape. The model incorporates the effects of Fermi level pinning at material interfaces, which arise due to interactions between interface states and electronic charge. The model can accurately predict the behavior of quantum framework properties in response to changes in growth conditions that affect the density of interface states. The underlying method of the computational framework is versatile and can be applied to various materials systems to optimize the design of new devices.

In this paper, we investigate the robustness of deep neural networks under localized manipulation during both training and testing phases. We allow an unlimited number of undisturbed regions and assess the effect of localized perturbations in terms of their size and intensity in a given dimension. Our study contributes three key findings: Firstly, we identify a theoretical limit on the training speed in the absence of localized perturbation handling, showing that the training time must increase exponentially with the dimension of the unperturbed data. Secondly, we demonstrate the effectiveness of local perturbation size in circumventing this limit, enabling efficient training in finite time. Lastly, we explore the local properties of data in a high-dimensional space and show that sampling a minimal set of points ensures dimensions that are effectively invariant under local perturbations, thus making localized perturbation handling unnecessary.

The use of Optimal Transport in various scientific and engineering fields has been hindered by its computational complexity of O(N^2 log N). Our research introduces a more efficient and fast-parallelizable algorithm for the Sinkhorn iteration, specifically designed for embedded systems. Our findings show that by limiting iterations to at most three, Fast Sinkhorn can accurately reproduce O(N^2 log N) precise solutions. Our proposed parallel algorithm achieves a computational complexity of O(N) and can be easily applied to specific problem types by utilizing special properties. Notably, when dealing with diagonal matrix structures, the algorithm requires only N multiplications and memory operations per iteration, while nearly dense matrices only differ in the number of operations per iteration. Our algorithm's parallelizability makes it suitable O(N) parallel complexity with a nearly-efficient constant factor of O(log N)/CPU cores. Notably, the Fast Sinkhorn algorithm outperforms OT-SGD, achieving performance gains of up to 200 times on systems with 32 CPU cores, and has been successfully applied to image denoising tasks with successful results.

The young star AU Mic has been the subject of multiple adolescent flares, 
studied through optical and UV observations. This research presents fresh UV 
data from AU Mic's quiescent state and two adolescent flares, captured by the Hubble Space Telescope. It's found that while the quiescent AU Mic's FUV emission is primarily due to its cool atmosphere, flares exhibit a FUV to optical ratio much higher than predicted by theoretical models. A hypothesis is presented that flares on AU Mic could be the result of magnetic field lines interacting with the star's magnetosphere and accretion stream, with neutral hydrogen ionized by the electric field accelerating electrons that produce the observed FUV emission. It's also proposed that quiescent AU Mic's FUV emission could be the result of the same mechanism occurring on its accretion columns, with FUV and X-ray emission produced by the collision of the high-velocity accretion stream with the star. It's proposed that while quiescent AU Mic's FUV emission is primarily due to its cool atmosphere, flares could be the result of magnetic field lines interacting with the star's magnetic field, with quiescent AU Mic's FUV emission primarily due to its cool atmosphere.
